Gene records found

gene symbol: BRCA1 [42]. gene name: BRCA1 [45]. This gene encodes a 190 kD nuclear phosphoprotein that plays a role in maintaining genomic stability, and it also acts as a tumor suppressor [51]. The BRCA1 gene contains 22 exons spanning about 110 kb of DNA [51]. The encoded protein combines with other tumor suppressors, DNA damage sensors, and signal transducers to form a large multi-subunit protein complex known as the BRCA1-associated genome surveillance complex (BASC) [51]. This gene product associates with RNA polymerase II, and through the C-terminal d [51].

pubmed title: HRDetect is a predictor of BRCA1 and BRCA2 deficiency based on mutational signatures [43]. pubmed title: BRCA1: An Endocrine and Metabolic Regulator [49]. pubmed title: Preneoplastic stromal cells promote BRCA1-mediated breast tumorigenesis [55]. pubmed title: Mechanism of BRCA1-BARD1 function in DNA end resection and DNA protection [60]. pubmed title: Targeting GPX4-mediated ferroptosis protection sensitizes BRCA1-deficient cancer cells to PARP inhibitors [65]. Approximately 1-5% of breast cancers are attributed to inherited mutations in BRCA1 or BRCA2 and are selectively sensitive to poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors [70]. In other cancer types, germline and/or somatic mutations in BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 (BRCA1/BRCA2) also confer selective sensitivity to PARP inhibitors [70]. Thus, assays to detect BRCA1/BRCA2-deficient tumors have been sought [70]. Recently, somatic substitution, insertion/deletion and rearrangement patterns, or 'mutational signatures', wer [70]. The breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility gene (BRCA1) is a tumor suppressor whose mutation has been associated with the development of breast, ovarian and, probably, other malignancies at young ages [72]. The BRCA1 gene product participates in multiple biological pathways including the DNA damage response, transcriptional control, cell growth and apoptosis [72]. Inactivating germline mutations of the BRCA1 gene can be detected in a substantial portion of families with inherited breast and/or ovarian c [72]. Women with germline BRCA1 mutations (BRCA1+/mut) have increased risk for hereditary breast cancer [74]. Cancer initiation in BRCA1+/mut is associated with premalignant changes in breast epithelium [74]. however, the role of the epithelium-associated stromal niche during BRCA1-driven tumor initiation remains unclear [74]. Here we show that the premalignant stromal niche promotes epithelial proliferation and mutant BRCA1-driven tumorigenesis in trans [74]. Using single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of human preneoplas [74]. DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair by homologous recombination is initiated by DNA end resection, a process involving the controlled degradation of the 5'-terminated strands at DSB sites1,2 [76]. The breast cancer suppressor BRCA1-BARD1 not only promotes resection and homologous recombination, but it also protects DNA upon replication stress1,3-9 [76]. BRCA1-BARD1 counteracts the anti-resection and pro-non-homologous end-joining factor 53BP1, but whether it functions in resection directly has been uncle [76]. BRCA1 is one of the most frequently-mutated tumor suppressor genes in ovarian and breast cancers [78]. Loss of BRCA1 triggers homologous recombination (HR) repair deficiency, consequently leading to genomic instability and PARP inhibitors (PARPi)-associated synthetic lethality [78]. Although, the roles of BRCA1 in DNA repair and replication have been extensively investigated, its tumor suppressive functions beyond genome safeguard remain poorly understood [78].
